analysis:
Examined both SelfUpdater excerpts, UpdateRecoveryState metadata, its patch and BASE source against the indexed threat model and supplied T-041 detail. SelfUpdater.swift:65 only widens the immutable clock closure from private to internal; production signature enforcement, hashing, staging, commit checks and network bounds are unchanged. No new key, prompt, cache, billing or authorization exposure is established by this visibility change.
UpdateRecoveryState.swift HEAD:305-319 introduces rollbackSource and permits completeRollback to replace a promoted current release as well as a pending candidate. It quarantines the replaced version, uses zero failures when no candidate remains, and retains the predecessor requirement. BASE:298-315 shows promotion previously cleared the candidate and thereby prevented this transition. The new transition is pure state arithmetic, not evidence of an unverified filesystem rollback or authorization bypass. No independently supported regression was found.
Integration should trace new rollbackSource/completeRollback callers and UpdateRecoveryStore's transaction completion: confirm promoted-release rollback only records success after the verified predecessor is restored, admission is appropriately drained, and failure/retry behavior cannot repeatedly restart or reinstall the quarantined release. Relevant contracts are T-043/A-018 availability and T-013/T-054/A-017 signed-build identity; local rollback must not imply coordinator serving qualification under TB-011. SelfUpdater.swift:172-175 and 253-263 use the maximum of process and recorded versions, so integration should reconcile that arithmetic with a persistent watchdog rolling back a promoted release. Those callers/store changes are outside this batch; their absence is a coverage limit, not a finding. T-041 cache crypto, scope and purge controls are not changed here.
